item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Friday Washington may carry out another military operation against Iran at a time when the war is nearing its eight month mark and as rise in fuel prices weigh on the US midterm elections . "We may do another little Epic Fury," Trump said in remarks at a rally in Florida as he spoke about the war. He did not elaborate. "Operation Epic Fury" is the name used by the US military for its war against Iran. Earlier on Friday, Trump said the US could end the war quickly but questioned whether Washington should seek a swift conclusion or allow the conflict to gradually wind down. Trump, who has [USN:L4N4061X8 TEXT:"offered shifting goals and timelines"] for the war, said earlier this month that the US would not launch an attack on Iran before the midterm elections in which control of Congress is up for grab. item.title: No hay evidencia de colocación de bandera palestina en la cima de la Torre Eiffel
item.description: No hay registro de que una bandera palestina haya ondeado en la cima de la Torre Eiffel en París, Francia, contrario a lo que muestra un clip compartido en redes sociales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: No hay registro de que una bandera palestina haya ondeado en la cima de la Torre Eiffel en París, Francia, contrario a lo que muestra un clip compartido en redes sociales. Estos son los detalles clave: Una publicación en Facebook dice que activistas del grupo Extinction Rebellion colocaron la bandera sobre el monumento. La publicación más antigua con el video fue compartida el 18 de octubre por el usuario de TikTok @jaranor.films, quien se describe como “creador de contenido Audiovisual & IA” y no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. La plataforma identificó el video como material con contenido multimedia generado por IA. Déborah Thiney-Masselin, portavoz de la Dirección General de la Policía Nacional de Francia, dijo en un correo el 20 de octubre que el clip compartido en redes sociales es falso y fue generado íntegramente por IA. Un análisis con la herramienta de verificación Meta Platforms determinó que la imagen probablemente fue editada o creada usando los modelos de IA de la empresa tecnológica. La herramienta detecta marcas de agua invisibles incrustadas en el medio generado. En el video, la bandera sobre la estructura contiene una estrella en el costado izquierdo, lo que no corresponde con la bandera palestina, y tampoco es visible un puente debajo, como lo muestra una captura de Google Street View. El 15 de mayo de 2026, miembros de Extinction Rebellion subieron a la Torre Eiffel para mostrar banderas palestinas en una planta inferior y no en la cima. Francia registra una ola de [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"manifestaciones"] que ha dado lugar a [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"enfrentamientos"] y daños materiales. La sociedad que administra la Torre Eiffel no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. Veredicto: Sin evidencia. No hay registro de que un grupo de personas haya colocado una bandera palestina en la cima de la Torre Eiffel. item.title: Video de senadora de Morena discutiendo es antiguo y no está relacionado con mensaje sobre aerolínea
item.description: Un video grabado en 2023 en el que la senadora Martha Lucía Mícher, del partido oficialista Morena, renuncia al partido durante una discusión en el Senado se comparte erróneamente en publicaciones que dicen que ocurrió en octubre de 2026, después de que la funcionaria hiciera comentarios sobre beneficios para clientes de Aeroméxico.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Un video grabado en 2023 en el que la senadora Martha Lucía Mícher, del partido oficialista Morena, renuncia al partido durante una discusión en el Senado se comparte erróneamente en publicaciones que dicen que ocurrió en octubre de 2026, después de que la funcionaria hiciera comentarios sobre beneficios para clientes de Aeroméxico. Publicaciones en línea que incluyen el video dicen en parte: “La Senadora Malú Micher de MORENA hace berrinche y amenaza con irse del partido ya que no la defendieron en su postura contra las salas VIP de Aeroméxico”. En el video, Mícher dice que iba a renunciar a Morena frente a integrantes de su bancada, entre ellas la entonces senadora Citlalli Hernández, hoy presidenta de la Comisión Nacional de Elecciones de Morena. Sin embargo, la versión más antigua del video vista por Reuters fue publicada por Político MX el 26 de octubre del 2023. Imágenes de la transmisión de la asamblea muestran el momento en que ocurrió el altercado, después de que la entonces presidenta de la Mesa Directiva, Ana Lilia Rivera, también de Morena, le negara la palabra a Mícher en la discusión de la Ley de Ingresos de 2024. Imágenes de la transmisión de la asamblea de ese día muestran el momento en que ocurrió el altercado, después de que la entonces presidenta de la Mesa Directiva, Ana Lilia Rivera, también de Morena, le negara la palabra a Mícher en la discusión de la Ley de Ingresos de 2024. La senadora Lilly Téllez compartió otro ángulo de la discusión. Horas después, Mícher dijo en su cuenta de X que había dialogado con Rivera y “se aclararon ideas”. La senadora no presentó una renuncia oficial en esa fecha y, al 23 de octubre de 2026, Mícher figura como integrante de Morena en el sitio web del Senado . POLÍTICAS DE AEROMÉXICO El 16 de octubre, la senadora expresó en X su inconformidad por los cambios en el acceso a los salones de Aeroméxico y dijo que pediría una reunión con ejecutivos de la empresa para que explicaran sus nuevas políticas. No hay información oficial a la fecha sobre negociaciones en el Senado con Aeroméxico. Según el sitio web de Aeroméxico, a partir del 1 de septiembre actualizó las condiciones de acceso a sus Salones Premier para socios Aeroméxico Rewards y dijo que los vuelos nacionales en Clase Premier ya no incluirían acceso a Salón Premier. El equipo de comunicación de Morena y Mícher no respondieron inmediatamente a una solicitud de comentarios. VEREDICTO Falta contexto. El video fue grabado durante una sesión del Senado el 26 de octubre de 2023, no muestra un registro actual tras comentarios de Martha Lucía Mícher sobre las políticas para usuarios de Aeroméxico. item.title: Kenya reports second death from Ebola
item.description: Kenya has recorded a second Ebola death, the health ministry said late on Friday, adding that the 65-year-old woman had developed symptoms during quarantine and was a close relative of a Kenyan man who died of Ebola earlier this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya has recorded a second Ebola death, the health ministry said late on Friday, adding that the 65-year-old woman had developed symptoms during quarantine and was a close relative of a Kenyan man who died of Ebola earlier this month. The outbreak, which started in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now been reported in four countries across eastern, central and western Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date. Kenya's first Ebola case was identified this month in a man who travelled from Congo to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5. Since then, Kenyan authorities have traced 135 contacts, all of whom were placed in quarantine, with nine cases confirmed. The Ebola victim who died on Friday evening was a direct contact of the index patient, the ministry said. "This loss brings the number of deaths to two among the nine confirmed cases. The remaining seven patients continue to receive care in the two isolation facilities," the ministry said, adding there was no evidence of community spread in the country. Late on Monday, the US State Department [USN:FWN4651IO TEXT:"advised"] Americans to reconsider travel to Kenya and raised its travel advisory level for the country because of health risks. On Tuesday, Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case, with officials scrambling to work out how and where the patient, who had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of Congo, contracted the disease. Ebola has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed more than 4,600 in Congo. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. Only people with symptoms can transmit the virus. The rare Ebola species behind the current outbreak has no approved treatment or vaccine.

item.title: Midterms: Your questions, answered
item.description: Over the summer, we asked you to submit your most pressing questions about the US midterm elections. Here are the answers and insights from our reporters.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax, Jason Lange, Nathan Layne, Rawan Yaghi
item.content:encoded: Over the summer, we asked you to submit your most pressing questions about the US midterm elections . You asked about voter eligibility checks, threats to election officials or results, the effects of redistricting and which races are most likely to determine control of Congress. Here are Reuters reporters’ answers to these questions, which were also published in the Politics US Newsletter . Similar questions have been combined and edited for clarity. If you have more questions related to the midterms or other topics related to US politics, write to campaigntrail@thomsonreuters.com . Q: Which national issues are having the greatest influence on competitive races? Answered by: Nathan Layne, Politics Reporter, and Jason Lange, Politics Data Reporter Our [USN:L6N43U101 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos polling"] suggests that [USN:L6N46017L TEXT:"rising prices"], exacerbated by the war with Iran, are having an outsized impact on the midterm environment. About half of voters say the cost of living is the single most important issue in the congressional elections, compared with roughly 1 in 5 who cite democratic norms and about 1 in 10 who point to immigration. That focus on inflation extends across the major expenses that dominate household budgets, from housing and healthcare to food and fuel. Gasoline prices, pushed higher by the conflict, and the elevated cost of grocery staples such as coffee and beef are particularly potent politically because voters encounter them regularly at the pump and checkout counter. Starting this past summer, our polling has shown that, for the first time in a decade, voters view Democrats as better stewards of the economy than Republicans. Against that backdrop, Republican strategists and party officials say they are seeking to frame the midterms as a choice between two parties, casting Democrats as increasingly influenced by socialist ideas, rather than a referendum on current economic conditions. Q: What are the most plausible paths for Democrats and Republicans to win control of the House and Senate in the 2026 midterm elections, and which races are most likely to determine the outcome? Answered by Jason Lange, Politics Data Reporter Democrats face an uphill fight to win[USN:L6N45U0XV TEXT:" the Senate"], where they need to pick up four seats. They would have to hold Michigan and New Hampshire – both tight races – while flipping four of six Republican-held seats in play: Alaska, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Iowa and Texas – the last two of which haven't elected Democrats to the Senate in over a decade. Republicans face more pressure in[USN:L6N45U0XS TEXT:" the House"], where their 218 members hold the smallest possible majority in the 435-seat chamber. About three dozen races nationwide are competitive. Democrats' best pickup chances include Republican-held seats in Nebraska's 2nd District, New Jersey's 7th and California's 48th, where district boundaries were redrawn to favor Democrats. Democrats must also defend Ohio's 9th and North Carolina's 1st, both redrawn to favor Republicans. Q: What procedures do states use to verify voter eligibility and citizenship, and what does the available evidence show about the frequency and detection of ineligible voting or other election fraud? Answered by Joseph Ax, National Affairs Correspondent Under federal law, every state must retain a statewide list of registered voters and perform regular maintenance on it to remove ineligible voters. In addition, US law requires first-time voters in federal elections who registered by mail to show some form of identification at the polls, such as a driver’s license, a paycheck or a utility bill. Many states have imposed additional, more stringent procedures to verify eligibility, such as photo ID requirements, and those policies vary significantly among states. Votes cast by mail, which have come under frequent baseless attacks from Trump as unreliable, are typically checked by comparing the signature on the envelope with the one on file. All available evidence indicates that ineligible voting, including noncitizen voting, is exceedingly rare. A Reuters investigation this year found just 129 cases in which noncitizens were federally charged with voting illegally; many appeared to stem from voter confusion or administrative errors, rather than intentional fraud. The conservative Heritage Foundation think tank maintains a voter fraud database that includes just 1,619 cases from 1982 to 2025, or one for every 817,625 votes cast in a presidential election during that time. Q: How are election officials preparing for threats to poll workers, misinformation, administrative disruptions or attempts to interfere with voting and vote counting? Answered by Peter Eisler , Ned Parker , Linda So and Mike Spector Reuters interviewed more than 50 state and local election officials from both political parties, including a dozen secretaries of state, the top election officials in their states. Nearly all said they are adopting new strategies to prepare for political interference, misinformation, cyberattacks and even threats of violence ahead of the midterms. Their efforts span jurisdictions large and small, in areas controlled by Republicans and Democrats. In Michigan, for example, state officials are advising local clerks on the appropriate response if the federal government demands access to voting machines. Preparations fall into three categories. Some election officials are hiring lawyers or seeking legal skills, as over a dozen interviewees said. Twice that many election officials said they are expanding public outreach and social media campaigns to counter misinformation around the reliability of mail-in voting or voting machines. Most of the interviewed officials said they are scrambling to fill gaps left by the Trump administration’s cuts to programs that help safeguard elections from cyberattacks and physical security threats. That includes ongoing work to fortify election offices with camera systems and bulletproof glass – a trend that began after Trump disputed his loss to Biden in the 2020 election, prompting violent threats by Trump supporters against election workers . Read our reporting on more specific examples of what election officials are doing in preparation for such potential scenarios in Wisconsin, North Carolina, Georgia, Michigan, Colorado and Maine. Q: How has redistricting affected the 2026 electoral map, and which maps or election practices are currently facing legal challenges? Answered by Joseph Ax, National Affairs Correspondent Nine states have new US House maps in place after the redistricting war that unfolded over the last year. Republicans were the clear winners: the party gained an advantage in 15 districts across those states, while Democrats improved their chances in only 6 districts. However, Democrats remain favored to win the House, with Trump’s weak approval ratings[USN:L1N4660I0 TEXT:" dragging down his party’s candidates"]. There are about 40 seats in play in November out of 435 nationwide, meaning that a small fraction of voters will likely determine which party controls the House. While some of the maps still face legal challenges, none of the litigation appears likely to alter any district lines ahead of November’s election. Reuters reporters Bianca Flowers , David Hood-Nuño and Ally J. Levine mapped how redistricting has affected communities in Memphis, Tennessee.

item.title: Argentine judge clears President Milei of wrongdoing in meme coin scandal
item.description: An Argentine federal judge dropped a criminal investigation into President Javier Milei and his sister Karina Milei over a meme coin scandal on Friday, finding no evidence of fraud, according to court records.
item.dc:creator: Leila Miller
item.content:encoded: An Argentine federal judge dropped a criminal investigation into President Javier Milei and his sister Karina Milei over a meme coin scandal on Friday, finding no evidence of fraud, according to court records. Federal judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi had been investigating Milei's role in promoting a cryptocurrency that crashed, looking into allegations of fraud in the coin's launch. Milei had recommended the little-known crypto coin Libra in a post on X in February 2025, kicking off a brief rally. He later deleted his post and denied having any link to the cryptocurrency, which soon plunged. Martinez de Giorgi wrote that, while Milei's institutional standing could have given the coin's launch "greater impact" when he posted about it on X, those things "do not, in themselves, amount to a fraudulent scheme." At the time of the currency's crash, Milei said he had acted "in good faith" and accused his political rivals of trying to take advantage of the situation. "I was not aware of the details of the project and once I found out, I decided to not continue giving it publicity," he said. Around $99 million worth of cryptocurrency was withdrawn from the marketplace of the coin by eight digital wallets linked to the crypto token's creator, blockchain researchers said. Argentina's fintech chamber at the time said the case could potentially be a "rug pull," in which the developers of a crypto token draw legitimate investments, pumping up the value, only to later dump their stake. The federal judge on Friday also dismissed an investigation into US businessman Hayden Davis, who had described himself as a "launch adviser" for the token and has acknowledged that he held close to $100 million after the crash. Davis has denied any wrongdoing.

item.title: Leclerc marca el mejor tiempo para Ferrari en las pruebas del GP de EEUU
item.description: Charles Leclerc lideró el viernes con Ferrari los entrenamientos del Gran Premio de Estados Unidos, con Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, muy cerca en segunda posición de cara a una carrera que podría convertirlo en el campeón del mundo más joven de la Fórmula 1.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Charles Leclerc lideró el viernes con Ferrari los entrenamientos del Gran Premio de Estados Unidos, con Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, muy cerca en segunda posición de cara a una carrera que podría convertirlo en el campeón del mundo más joven de la Fórmula 1. Leclerc marcó el mejor tiempo, con un minuto y 35,291 segundos, en la segunda sesión en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin tras haber registrado la vuelta más rápida en la primera tanda con marca de 1:36,052 a bordo de su monoplaza mejorado en una pista llena de baches. Antonelli, de 20 años y que debe ganar el domingo para tener una primera oportunidad de hacerse con el título, quedó quinto en la primera sesión, en la que Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, fue el más cercano a Leclerc, ganador de la carrera en 2024. El italiano, que se quejó de que su asiento se movía, mejoró hasta el segundo puesto y terminó el día a 0,042 del mejor tiempo. Verstappen, ganador en Austin el año pasado, busca su tercera victoria consecutiva tras las de Singapur y Malasia. Terminó la segunda sesión en el tercer escalón, a 0,189 de Leclerc, con Lewis Hamilton cuarto con Ferrari y George Russell quinto para Mercedes. Russell recibió una bandera de advertencia por un incidente con Leclerc que provocó que el monegasco se saliera de la pista al principio de la segunda sesión, pero los comisarios decidieron no tomar ninguna medida adicional. El vigente campeón de McLaren, Lando Norris, fue el tercero más rápido en la tanda inicial, a 0,245 del mejor tiempo, y luego quedó séptimo, por detrás de Liam Lawson, de Racing Bulls. "Creo que Lando es, sin duda, mucho más rápido de lo que indica su tiempo de vuelta", declaró el jefe de McLaren, Zak Brown, a la cadena Sky Sports. Gabriel Bortoleto, de Audi; Arvid Lindblad, de Racing Bulls; y Franco Colapinto, de Alpine, han recibido penalizaciones en la parrilla por cambios en sus unidades de potencia. Lindblad bajará cinco puestos desde la posición en la que se clasifique el sábado, Colapinto 10 y Bortoleto, 20. Williams pareció tener dificultades, con Carlos Sainz en el puesto 20 y Alex Albon en el 22 en la segunda sesión de entrenamientos. "El coche es un desastre ahora mismo, un desastre. No tengo confianza en la parte trasera", dijo Sainz por la radio del equipo. El circuito ha sido objeto de críticas por parte de algunos pilotos debido a lo accidentado que se ha vuelto. "Probablemente sea el circuito más bacheado que hemos tenido en lo que va de año. Es complicado, pero estoy seguro de que sabremos adaptarnos", declaró Pierre Gasly, de Alpine, a la cadena Sky Sports.

item.title: Leclerc fastest for Ferrari in US GP Friday practice
item.description: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led the way in US Grand Prix practice on Friday, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli a close second ahead of a race that could make him Formula One's youngest champion.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led the way in US Grand Prix practice on Friday, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli a close second ahead of a race that could make him Formula One's youngest champion. Leclerc set the pace of one minute 35.291 seconds in a sunny second practice at Austin's Circuit of the Americas after also lapping fastest in the earlier session with a time of 1:36.052 in his upgraded car on a bumpy track. Antonelli, the 20-year-old who must win on Sunday to have a first chance of taking the title, was fifth in session one when Red Bull's Max Verstappen was closest to 2024 winner Leclerc. The Italian, who complained about his seat moving, then improved to second place and ended the day 0.042 off the pace. Verstappen, winner in Austin last year, is chasing his third successive victory after Singapore and Malaysia. He ended second practice as the third fastest and 0.189 off Leclerc with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton fourth and Mercedes' George Russell fifth. Russell had a black-and-white warning flag for an incident with Leclerc that led to the Monegasque going off track early in the second session, but stewards decided against any further action. McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris was third fastest, 0.245 off the pace, in first practice and then seventh later on and behind Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. "I think Lando is definitely a lot quicker than his lap time," McLaren boss Zak Brown told Sky Sports television. "He didn't get his third sector in. His first two sectors were very strong. "So I think we are much quicker than we looked. I think Ferrari's lap time, Mercedes' lap time, there or thereabouts." Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto all collected grid drops for changes to their power units. Lindblad will drop five places from wherever he qualifies on Saturday, Colapinto 10 places and Bortoleto 20. Williams looked to be struggling, with Carlos Sainz 20th and Alex Albon 22nd in practice two. "The car is a mess right now. It's a mess. I have no confidence in the rear," said Sainz over the team radio.

item.title: US Justice Dept sues to block possible Alaska election of Democrat to Senate
item.description: Control of the US Senate could come down to Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan is running a closely contested race against Democrat Mary Peltola.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Thursday sued to preemptively block Alaska from certifying the results of its US Senate race if the Republican incumbent candidate loses by a narrow margin, saying voters could be confused because two Republicans on the ballot have almost identical names. The lawsuit signals the willingness of President Donald Trump's administration to contest the results of the November 3 midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress. Trump's administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including both Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the moves as federal overreach. Control of the US Senate could come down to Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan is running a closely contested race against Democrat Mary Peltola. The Justice Department's lawsuit , filed in federal court in Anchorage, takes issue with the presence of a third contender in the race, another Republican named Dan J. Sullivan Jr, alleging he is running "with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him." The lawsuit asks a federal judge to block the certification of an outcome "that may be impacted by voter confusion," so that there can be "an investigation to determine whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan." Trump told reporters on Friday that he supported the lawsuit, saying "I'm the one that said do it." A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that the agency is taking "necessary steps to ensure that this frivolous candidacy does not undermine the integrity of Alaska’s election or the will of its voters.” Election officials around the country have told Reuters they are preparing for potential federal interference in November’s elections, including legal challenges and disputes over voting that could disrupt certification of the results. Trump has a long history of challenging election outcomes and encouraging supporters to contest results he views as unfavorable. Election law experts said the Justice Department's lawsuit has no merit and seeks relief not allowed under federal law. "In short, like many Department letters over the last few years, it is designed to win the press release rather than the litigation," wrote Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller in a blog post , adding that "the legal argument is one of the worst ones I’ve ever seen." Trump's administration "has absolutely no authority to tell Alaska when or how to certify the results of its Senate election," said David Becker of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, a nonpartisan group that advises election officials, adding that "this issue has already been fully litigated by Alaska's courts." The unelected Sullivan, a former US Forest Service worker and elementary school teacher, filed to run as a candidate on May 29 seeking to unseat Senator Dan S. Sullivan and "put Alaska first," according to his campaign website, which advertised "Dan Sullivan Challenges Dan Sullivan for US Senate Seat." Dan J. Sullivan has denied in interviews with US news outlets that his aim is to cause confusion or divert votes from Dan S. Sullivan. The Alaska Supreme Court in June permitted the unelected Sullivan to appear on the ballot. He will appear without a party designation next to his name, while the senator will be listed as the Republican incumbent. Trump's [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"approval rating"] has fallen to a record low, hit by rising diesel and gasoline prices and a conflict in the Middle East that has proven deeply unpopular with voters. Public opinion polls suggest Republicans may lose control of one or both houses of Congress, which would likely limit Trump's ability to enact his policies in the final two years of his presidency.

item.title: Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28 and once again by end-March: Reuters poll
item.description: The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Nushaiba Iqbal
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters. Inflation rose to [USN:L6N4620VU TEXT:"3.1%"] in September, only barely overshooting the BoC's target range of 1% to 3%. But the central bank's latest [USN:BCLJLEM2I TEXT:"business outlook survey"] showed sharply rising inflation expectations in the run-up to a recent breakdown in trade talks with the United States, Canada's main export destination. Quarterly inflation forecasts from the bank, also due next week, are likely to be [USN:L6N463037 TEXT:"revised higher"], BoC Governor Tiff Macklem told reporters in remarks Saturday that markets interpreted as a hint a rate rise is coming. Interest rate futures have moved from pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike in October to around a three-in-four likelihood. Many economists this week changed their view from a hold to a hike, citing those remarks from Macklem. "What changed the tone in the governor's public comments on the weekend and what changed our view on Monday is the same source, and that is the responses from the BoC's business outlook and consumer surveys," said Royce Mendes, managing director and head of macro strategy at Desjardins. "So presumably the governor had seen the results before they were published more broadly on Monday. And I would assume that informed his public commentary," Mendes said. "The survey responses...suggest there are more serious inflationary pressures coming." Nineteen of 34 economists surveyed in the October 21-23 poll, or 56% of them, said the BoC will hike its overnight rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50%, its first move in a year. This is a clear reversal from the previous poll, when 80% of respondents forecast the bank would hold its rate at 2.25% until the end of 2026, and two-thirds of them forecast a hold until the end of March 2027. Those economists who forecast no move next week mainly cited a weak economy and subdued inflation pressures despite soaring oil prices , which hit $117 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday. Sixteen of 29 respondents, a 55% majority, also forecast one more rise before March 2027, after which policymakers would hold the overnight rate at 2.75%, poll medians showed. If correct, it will be the shortest BoC policy tightening campaign in 30 years. But even a short series of hikes would bring the BoC into a widening group of central banks that have opted for tighter monetary policy in response to persistent inflation emerging as a result of the US-led [USN:L6N46718Z TEXT:"war"] with Iran that began in February. Among major central banks, only the BoC and the Bank of England — which is [USN:L6N4610Q9 TEXT:"widely expected"] to raise rates at its early November meeting — have not yet begun to raise rates. But many say the BoC will need to be measured with the pace of rate increases given other risks to the economy. Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates and macro strategist at BMO, said: "They'd rather make the mistake of hiking a little bit too early, which means maybe they have to hike a little bit less at the end of the day than falling behind the curve, which is what happened in 2021-2022, and they don't want to repeat that mistake.” Economic growth likely slowed to 1.9% last quarter from 3.3% [USN:L6N44O17F TEXT:"in Q2"] and is forecast at 1.3% in the current one before accelerating next year, poll medians showed. The economy will grow 1.0% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, the survey found. Inflation will average 2.8% for 2026 as a whole, falling to 2.3% in 2027, poll medians showed. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: Mark Cuban says AI hack agents are like cockroaches, but can be controlled
item.description: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said on Friday that he is "not a doomer" about artificial intelligence and that companies should be able to use the technology to protect themselves from AI-driven hacks by agents that he compared to cockroaches.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Humer
item.content:encoded: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said on Friday that he is "not a doomer" about artificial intelligence and that companies should be able to use the technology to protect themselves from AI-driven hacks by agents that he compared to cockroaches. "It's like the cockroach thing, right? You build a new house, you get the guys to come out and spray... the one thing I don't want is cockroaches in my house ever. But the cockroaches find a way to get in because there's zillions of them, right? And then if there's one gets in, there's more that are going to get in, and that's kind of the way AI works," Cuban said, speaking at Reuters Total Health. "It's all brute force acts, and if it's brute force on that side with the bad guys, you can also use brute force with the good guys," he said. Cuban, famous for his role on business reality show "Shark Tank" and his involvement in the Dallas Mavericks NBA team, ventured into healthcare when he started the online pharmacy Cost Plus Drug Company in 2022 with a standard pricing scheme: the cost it pays for the drug, plus 15%. In May, Cost Plus signed on with TrumpRx.gov, a website created by the Trump administration selling discounted weight-loss drugs. But the company has also moved into manufacturing. In 2025, it began making sterile injectable drugs typically used in hospitals in its own compounding manufacturing facility. Cuban said the company has built smaller, tractor-trailer-sized manufacturing facilities he calls "pods" that can be used separately or together to manufacture many kinds of drugs, including generics and treatments for rare diseases. He said the pods would eventually be Cost Plus Drugs' biggest business and would allow medicines to be manufactured closer to where they are needed in the event of a disaster, because they're portable. One holdup, Cuban said, has been getting regulators from the US Food and Drug Administration to sign off on the pods. "We're talking to the FDA to try to get approval," he said without outlining the complications. "They're working hard to try to figure it out." Cuban campaigned for Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris in 2024 and has supported Democratic candidate James Talarico for US Senate this year in Texas. He said two items he believes the US government should immediately put in place to help lower healthcare costs would be that all payments made out of pocket should count towards patients' deductibles and that taxpayer-funded health contracts should be public without redactions. Still, Cuban said he did not believe Democrats were necessarily better than Republicans on healthcare. "None of them know what they're doing," he said.

item.title: NFL closes Paris pop-up shop ahead of planned protests
item.description: The NFL will close its Paris pop-up shop on Saturday because of planned demonstrations in the French capital ahead of this weekend's regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, the league said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NFL will close its Paris pop-up shop on Saturday because of planned demonstrations in the French capital ahead of [USN:L1N4690K8 TEXT:"this weekend's regular-season game"] between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, the league said on Friday. The store on Rue Saint-Merri had been operating as part of events surrounding Sunday's game at the Stade de France, the first NFL regular-season contest to be held in France. "The NFL Shop on Rue Saint-Merri will be closed tomorrow Saturday 24 October, due to potential accessibility issues," the league said in a statement. The street is located in Paris' fourth arrondissement, in the city centre. The league said the shop would remain open until 8 p.m. local time on Friday and that an alternative NFL pop-up store would operate at the Stade de France on Saturday. The Steelers had already cancelled a fan event scheduled for the weekend at a bar on Place de la Bastille amid concerns over the demonstrations. France experienced some of its worst urban unrest in recent years last weekend, prompting President Emmanuel Macron's government to tighten restrictions on protests as authorities prepared for the possibility of further violence on Saturday. Sunday's game will take place in Saint-Denis, about 10 km north of Paris centre, with organisers continuing preparations despite disruption elsewhere in the city. Concerns over renewed unrest have also led several major cultural venues, including the Louvre, to close on Saturday, while the Art Basel Paris fair will remain shut throughout the weekend.

item.title: Senator says planned Meta commercial terms update could harm US businesses
item.description: US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' (META.O) plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators. Blackburn, who is chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology and the Law, said the updated terms "indicate Meta is attempting to exploit American creators and businesses by granting itself sweeping authority to scrape content from any website associated with Facebook and Instagram business accounts." Earlier on Friday, Meta said it would delay the implementation of updated commercial terms from October 30 until November 20, so it can address concerns from publishers and digital advertisers. EU and UK antitrust authorities have received [USN:L6N46817D TEXT:"complaints"] about the new commercial terms, which publishers and digital advertisers said would give Meta unlimited rights to use their content for its AI services. Meta has rejected the claims. Blackburn said that Meta previously revised its terms to remove an explicit reference to AI training but said the changes did not go far enough. She added that the revised language authorizes extensive scraping of external websites and permits Meta to “develop” its business products with collected content. "Without clear restrictions on how that information may be used, including whether it may be incorporated into AI systems, Meta’s revisions offer little assurance that creators’ intellectual property will be protected," Blackburn said. She added: "This is particularly troubling for American news publishers, creators, and small businesses that rely on Meta’s platforms to reach their audiences and customers." Asked for comment on Blackburn's letter, Meta on Friday noted it had delayed the change and said the revised terms apply only to its ads and business products and that it is not changing how it uses web crawlers. "These updates don't give us new rights to supersede such preferences and this isn’t about scraping news sites," the company said, noting that "content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences." Publishers worldwide are ramping up fights with AI companies using their content without permission to train large language models, underscoring the clash between copyright owners and those citing fair-use arguments. "Meta must withdraw the updated Commercial Terms and come to the table to protect the content of creators and publishers across the country," Blackburn said. "American creators and small businesses are not a free source of content for Meta to exploit."

item.title: Top LNG exporter QatarEnergy in talks to buy US LNG from Woodside's Louisiana plant
item.description: QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Curtis Williams, Marwa Rashad
item.content:encoded: QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy (WDS.AX) to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters. If a final agreement is reached, the long-term deal could see QatarEnergy buying LNG from the 16.5 mtpa export facility for between 15 and 20 years, one of the people said. Woodside Energy said on Friday it does not respond to market speculation, while QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. QatarEnergy has been buying LNG on the spot market from US exporters to supply some of its customers due to the ongoing blockage of the Strait of Hormuz as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Tehran’s strikes this year have sharply curtailed shipping. The company is also a 70% owner of the Golden Pass LNG facility being developed in Louisiana, which when complete will have the capacity to export up to 18 mtpa of LNG. On Thursday, Cheniere Energy (LNG.N) reported it had reached a long-term agreement to supply QatarEnergy with 4 mtpa of LNG. Two million metric tons per year will be sourced from Cheniere’s Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana, and another 2 mpta will come from its Corpus Christi terminal in Texas. Reuters also [USN:L1N468185 TEXT:"reported"] on Thursday that QatarEnergy is in advanced talks with Venture Global (VG.N) for a long-term supply deal to buy at least 3 million metric tons of LNG per year. Venture Global and Woodside's Louisiana LNG are the US suppliers with the most uncommitted LNG capacity. Louisiana LNG is said to be asking for a premium for liquefaction fees that exceed $2.50 per mmBtu and are above the average US market prices because of contract flexibility, offering potential buyers shorter contracts in return for higher prices, two people told Reuters.

item.title: Trump ends tariffs on some Canadian products, aiming to help Senator Collins
item.description: With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight reelection battle, President Donald Trump signed an order on Friday to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit companies from the state.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight reelection battle, President Donald Trump signed an order on Friday to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit companies from the state. The Republican president's hefty tariffs on Canada have caused friction with the US neighbor to the north while creating problems for American businesses in Maine and other states that rely on certain Canadian goods. With the November 3 US midterm elections looming and Republicans fighting to retain control of Congress, [USN:L6N3YF150 TEXT:"Senator Susan Collins"] had urged the White House to address tariffs on products affecting Maine companies and farmers. Trump's order exempted plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, and packing crates and boxes, as well as fresh and dried seaweed, the White House said. The changes take effect on October 30, four days before the election. Trump added a number of Canadian products to the 50% tariff list to offset the tariff relief provided in his order, including carpets, paints, shampoos, cocoa powder, wooden coffins, ice cream sticks, air-conditioning machines, chest freezers, archery equipment and canoes. Collins said the relief will aid Maine's blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers. "These producers are a vital part of our state's economy and support our rural and coastal communities," Collins said. "Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense." [USN:L6N43P103 TEXT:"Democrat Troy Jackson"] is seeking to oust Collins in next month's election in a race that polls indicate is very close. The two sparred over tariffs at an October 6 debate. "Trump's trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers," Jackson said on Friday after Trump's action. "Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire." Trump in August imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian imports, which took effect after talks between the two countries collapsed. Canada retaliated in September with tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on $20 billion in US goods. Canada and the United States have been engaged in a standoff over the tariffs since Trump imposed them. Trump on Friday asserted that Canada is working on a deal. Republican candidates in northern US border states most affected by the tariffs, including Maine and Michigan, are trying to strike a balance between appealing to Trump's loyal conservative base and winning over independent voters. 'REFINING THE SCOPE' In a statement concerning Trump's action on Friday, White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said the president "continues to address Canada's discriminatory treatment of US commerce" and that the new moves are "further refining the scope" of the previously announced tariffs. The Canadian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The economies of Michigan and Maine have long been intertwined with that of Canada, covering everything from auto parts to lumber to fruit-picking equipment. Republicans may need to win closely contested Senate races in both states in order to maintain their majority in the chamber. "Trump's desperate, 11th-hour attempt to save Susan Collins' political career is an admission that American voters are rejecting his toxic tariff policies. No one will forget how Trump raised prices on thousands of products American families need by slapping trade taxes on goods from around the world," Senator Ron Wyden, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, said in a statement on Friday. Trump's threat in September to block Canadian jet maker Bombardier (BBDb.TO) from the US market became a political issue in Kansas, where the company employs 1,500 workers in Wichita. Trump dropped the threatened ban this week after calls from Kansas lawmakers including Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who also is locked in a tough reelection race.

item.title: Hugo Boss set to become Frasers subsidiary as stake crosses 50%
item.description: Fashion group Hugo Boss will become a subsidiary of Mike Ashley-controlled Frasers after the British retailer on Friday raised its stake in the German company to more than 50%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fashion group Hugo Boss (BOSSn.DE) will become a subsidiary of Mike Ashley-controlled Frasers (FRAS.L) after the British retailer on Friday raised its stake in the German company to more than 50%. Frasers, which made a [USN:L6N43B0GF TEXT:"failed €2 billion takeover bid"] for the German fashion house in June, said it had bought a further 198,666 Hugo Boss shares for about €7.6 million ($8.51 million), taking its total stake to about 34.5 million shares, or 50.08%. Hugo Boss' earnings, assets and liabilities are expected to be consolidated into Frasers' accounts as the stake passed 50%, the British firm said. A Hugo Boss spokesperson said the company had taken note of Frasers' latest stake increase, but said that crossing the 50% threshold would not have any major implications. Frasers, which has been pushing in to the premium and luxury space and ramping up its pursuit of the underperforming German designer known for its boxy men's suits, said crossing the 50% stake threshold was in the best interests of its investors. Since Hugo Boss rejected a [USN:L6N43B0GF TEXT:"€38-per-share cash offer"] as "financially inadequate," the company's chairman has stepped down and Frasers CEO Michael Murray has become the chairman of its supervisory board while the British company has steadily raised its stake. The stake purchase was funded from existing cash resources, Frasers said. Frasers shares closed 0.3% higher on Friday, while Hugo Boss ended 0.8% lower. ($1 = 0.8935 euro)

item.title: BP, Louisiana agree to Deepwater Horizon settlement payout, resolve coastal cases
item.description: BP announced a deal on Friday that provides Louisiana an accelerated, lump-sum $350 million payment to resolve claims over the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and that also settles long-running coastal damage litigation by local parishes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) announced a deal on Friday that provides Louisiana an accelerated, lump-sum $350 million payment to resolve claims over the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and that also settles long-running coastal damage litigation by local parishes. • BP agreed in 2015 to pay up to $18.7 billion to the federal government and five states to resolve claims arising out of the oil spill. That money includes $4.9 billion payable over 18 years to settle economic and other claims by the states. • While Louisiana had been owed $373 million over the next seven years, the state will now receive a single $350 million payment. • BP said remaining coastal zone lawsuits by Louisiana parishes will be resolved. It did not provide further details. • "We have now disposed of claims and settled with all but one of the major defendants in these coastal cases," Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry, a Republican, said in a statement distributed by BP.

item.title: Judge puts off decision on Charlie Kirk murder trial date, media reports
item.description: A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk more than a year ago, media reported.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hay
item.content:encoded: A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent [USN:L2N3UX161 TEXT:"right-wing activist Charlie Kirk"] more than a year ago, media reported. At a hearing in Provo, Utah, District Court Judge Tony Graf heard arguments from defense lawyers, prosecutors and a lawyer for Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, before saying he needed to consider their positions. He set a new hearing for November 9, television station KUTV reported. Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to seven counts, including aggravated murder, for allegedly shooting Kirk as he held one of his trademark debates at Utah Valley University in Orem. Robinson's lawyers expect a six-to-seven-month trial. Robinson's attorneys had asked for a late 2029 trial to give them time to challenge Utah's request for the death penalty, gather additional evidence and seek a change of venue, among other issues, according to a scheduling memo. Prosecutors, meanwhile, sought a date of January 31, 2028 to start what they expect to be a 17-week trial, according to their scheduling memo . In a separate filing , Erika Kirk said the defense request was "grossly out of line with comparable cases" and requested the trial start no later than October 4, 2027. Shortly before Friday's hearing, President Donald Trump, with whom Kirk had been allied, slammed Graf's handling of the case in a social media post , saying it should be tried within a month and Graf was asking "questions that people already know the answer to." Kirk was a polarizing figure in US politics. He was admired by conservatives for mobilizing young voters around his Christian and right-wing views. Opponents criticized his rhetoric on immigration, race, gender and other social issues. Prosecutors [USN:L6N43V09L TEXT:"allege"] Robinson targeted Kirk for his opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights. Defense attorney Richard Novak has said Kirk spoke "hatefully" about people who did not have traditional gender identities or were not heterosexual, but there was no evidence Robinson opposed those views.

item.title: Trump and Burnham discuss North Sea oil, Ukraine and Falklands
item.description: US President Donald Trump said he discussed opening up North Sea oil during a conversation with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, as well as touching on the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine "very lightly."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said he discussed opening up North Sea oil during a conversation with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, as well as touching on the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine "very lightly." "They're opening up the North Sea oil," Trump told reporters at the White House before departing for a campaign trip to Florida ahead of the November 3 midterm US elections. "I've been after them to do that for two years... Andy is getting it done." On Wednesday, Trump praised Britain's approval of the [USN:L8N46707X TEXT:"Jackdaw North Sea gas field"], a decision that ended years of legal and political wrangling, though British officials said a decision about the bigger Rosebank oilfield was yet to be made. Burnham's office said in a statement that the two leaders agreed the Jackdaw approval would bring "significant benefits" to Britain. They also welcomed continued cooperation between British and US companies, particularly on nuclear power. Burnham also raised the topic of oil exploration off the [USN:L6N45F0WA TEXT:"Falkland Islands,"] a largely self-governing British overseas territory whose sovereignty Argentina has long disputed. Burnham spoke about the economic consequences for Britain and the US of what he described as Argentina's coercive [USN:S0N44M029 TEXT:"measures"] seeking to halt the drilling and reiterated the importance of respecting the islanders' right to develop their natural resources, Downing Street added. On Ukraine, Burnham underlined the importance of Kyiv having full access to [USN:L6N4690ZQ TEXT:"Starlink"] to defend itself against Russia and welcomed Trump's efforts to bring Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table. The leaders agreed to work with international partners to end the bloodshed, the statement said. The leaders also discussed the Middle East, with Burnham reaffirming Britain's support for Saudi Arabia in the face of [USN:L1N46809Q TEXT:"Houthi attacks"].

item.title: PwC confirms cybersecurity incident involving employee learning records
item.description: PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data.
item.dc:creator: A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data. A PwC global spokesperson said "the affected site does not house client data, sensitive personal data or financial information. Once we learned of this incident we acted promptly to secure the environment and conduct a thorough review." The incident "does not impact our network or any of our operations," the spokesperson said. A cyber extortion group called "Everest" claimed responsibility for the data breach in a message posted to its website October 22, according to cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The message included a countdown timer with five days remaining, and a message indicating the data would be released if a deal could not be reached. Everest claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of data that included "regional HR and learning exports, integration documentation, software components and PwC e-learning courses." The data contains information "about individuals and their organisational and employment history," Everest said, including names, email addresses, telephone numbers, addresses and other details. The PwC spokesperson declined to comment on the amount of data stolen or the veracity of the hacking group's claims.

item.title: Bank of Italy calls for digital asset investments by banks despite uncertainty
item.description: As the financial system turns increasingly digital, banks must resist the temptation to delay investments until they know which technology will prevail, a senior Bank of Italy official said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As the financial system turns increasingly digital, banks must resist the temptation to delay investments until they know which technology will prevail, a senior Bank of Italy official said on Friday. Waiting could help lenders save money in the short term, but it "also has costs when it delays learning or the creation of future opportunities," Bank of Italy Deputy Governor Chiara Scotti said in the text of a speech Scotti said banks should target investments that lend themselves to usefulness across different scenarios and support institutions' learning process Only by experimenting can banks understand how best to adapt the new digital technologies to their business, she said "It makes sense to start on a limited scale... flexibility and staged commitment can reconcile caution with innovation, without requiring an early bet on a single technological path," she said Scotti said it was still unclear how widely tokenisation — a technology that turns bank deposits into digital tokens that can be moved on blockchain-based networks — would spread, but banks must act if they are to preserve their role as issuers of private money

item.title: Carney dismisses US accusations of Canadian election interference
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday dismissed accusations that Canada planned to interfere in next month's US midterm elections and said he was disappointed in comments made by the American ambassador.
item.dc:creator: Maria Cheng
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday dismissed accusations that Canada planned to interfere in next month's US midterm elections and said he was disappointed in comments made by the American ambassador. Carney's remarks underline the chilly state of bilateral relations since Canada [USN:L1N44I0GP TEXT:"walked"] away from talks on a possible trade deal in late August, citing unreasonable US demands. The US embassy in Canada on Wednesday said Ottawa "brushes off concerns about potential interference in US elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics." A week earlier, Ambassador Pete Hoekstra had told a podcast that his message to Canadians was to "keep your nose out of American politics." Carney said Canada had no intention of interfering in the November 3 elections. "There is no merit to these claims," he told reporters during an official visit to Turkey. "I'm disappointed their envoy sees that as his role to make these suggestions." US President Donald Trump has imposed a raft of tariffs on imports from Canada and frequently suggests he could annex the country. His approval rating at home is at record lows, and polls suggest his Republican Party will do [USN:L1N4670HR TEXT:"badly"] in the midterms that will determine control of the US Congress. Asked whether he thought Trump could use poor election results as an excuse to impose more tariffs on Canada, Carney said he did not think that was likely. The trade talks that collapsed in August had been intended in part to cut some of the tariffs. Carney reiterated that Canada was in no rush to sign a deal and, for the first time, suggested Ottawa might wait till Trump's term was over. "If it has to be months from now or longer than that, or another administration before a proper deal comes into place, we will do that," he said. The trip to Turkey is part of a campaign to reduce Canada's heavy reliance on the US economy. "It's absolutely clear where I stand, where Canada stands, where Canadians stand. We will never be the 51st state. We are going our own way," Carney said.

item.title: Plazas en Brasil ajustan posiciones antes de balotaje; inversores ya miran a la Fed
item.description: Los mercados financieros de Brasil avanzaron el viernes, mientras los inversores ajustaban posiciones previo a lo que se espera sea un reñido balotaje presidencial, con las monedas de la región cotizando mixtas con la mira ya puesta también en la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Los mercados financieros de Brasil avanzaron el viernes, mientras los inversores ajustaban posiciones previo a lo que se espera sea un reñido balotaje presidencial, con las monedas de la región cotizando mixtas con la mira ya puesta también en la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal. * El real brasileño ganó un 0,97% a 4,9896 por dólar, para marcar un avance del 1,64% en la semana; al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) sumó preliminarmete un 0,76% a 205.679 puntos. * Los inversores ajustaron posiciones de cara a la segunda vuelta presidencial del domingo en la mayor economía de América Latina, con la expectativa de que el senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro supere al presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro lidera los sondeos de opinión, aunque la ventaja se fue estrechando en los últimos días. * Una encuesta de Datafolha divulgada la noche del jueves mostró que ambos se encontraban igualados con 50% de los votos válidamente emitidos. La semana pasada el candidato opositor contaba con un 51% y el actual mandatario con 49% con la muestra de votos válidos, que no considera los blancos, los nulos ni los indecisos. * El senador ganó la primera vuelta, aunque la mayoría de las encuestas mostraba una ventaja de Lula. * Los otros mercados también reaccionaban más tranquilos luego de que en la víspera fueran golpeados por una búsqueda de seguridad por parte de los inversores. * Los precios del crudo volvieron a subir con fuerza en la sesión, con el contrato referencial Brent superando los 116 dólares por barril, alimentando los temores sobre una inflación relacionada con la energía que al parecer ya se traspasa a la economía en general. * La Fed culmina el miércoles su reunión de dos días y aunque los mercados descuentan que mantendrá sin cambios las tasas de interés, buscarán pistas en el comunicado y en la posterior conferencia de prensa del jefe del organismo, Kevin Warsh, sobre futuras decisiones. Los operadores esperan un alza de 25 puntos básicos en diciembre. * El peso mexicano subía por la tarde un 0,24%, a 18,6547 unidades por dólar, tras un descenso en las primeras operaciones, aunque anotó su séptima semana consecutiva de descenso, golpeado por un desmantelamiento de operaciones de carry trade ante expectativas de una disminución del diferencial de tasas entre Estados Unidos y México. * Mientras, el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, cotizó prácticamente estable a 69.879,62 puntos. De todas formas terminó la semana con una leve alza. * A nivel local, la [USN:AQN2MPJKQ TEXT:"actividad económica"] moderó su ritmo de crecimiento en agosto, aunque menos de lo previsto. El dato antecede a la divulgación, la próxima semana, de las cifras oportunas del PIB del tercer trimestre. * "Estos resultados, en conjunto con la información disponible de julio y los datos conocidos de septiembre, llevan a prever que la actividad económica crecerá un 1,0% trimestral en el tercer trimestre de 2026, equivalente a un avance del 3,4% interanual. Considerando esto, revisamos al alza nuestro pronóstico para el PIB de todo el 2026 a 1,9%, desde 1,4%", dijo Banorte. * El peso colombiano se apreció un 0,91% a 3.145 unidades por dólar, en su segunda sesión de alzas; al tiempo que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el COLCAP (.COLCAP) , repuntó un 0,46% a 2.540,1 puntos. * "La ganancia local estuvo asociada al aumento de los precios del petróleo, principal producto de exportación del país, y a la expectativa de flujos de dólares provenientes del endeudamiento externo esperado del Gobierno en las próximas semanas", explicó el Banco de Bogotá en una nota. * El peso chileno , cerró las operaciones con una caída del 0,73%, en 993,50/993,80 unidades por dólar y acumuló un retroceso del 0,97% durante la semana. Asimismo, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , moderó sus descensos previos y cayó un 0,31%, a 10.746,36 puntos. * El peso mayorista argentino bajó un leve 0,1% a 1.529,5 por dólar, con la intervención diaria del banco central (BCRA) que acumuló compras por 270 millones de dólares en el transcurso de la semana, contabilizados los 42 millones adquiridos este viernes. Las reservas de la autoridad monetaria suman 50.203 millones de dólares en base al último dato oficial provisorio. * El índice líder MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires, en tanto, saltó un 4,29% al cierre en línea a los 'ADRs' de Nueva York. * La moneda peruana, el sol , se depreció un 0,12% a 3,4470/3,4490 unidades por dólar y cayó un 0,29% en la semana. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) cayó un 0,22% 1.513,47 puntos.

item.title: Wall Street cierra en baja para terminar complicada semana
item.description: El Dow Jones y el S&P 500 cerraron a la baja el viernes, mientras que las acciones tecnológicas se estabilizaron tras una semana turbulenta para el sector de la inteligencia artificial, que ha sido el principal motor del mercado, con los inversores atentos a una intensa agenda de resultados corporativos y a la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Lewis Krauskopf, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: El Dow Jones y el S&P 500 cerraron a la baja el viernes, mientras que las acciones tecnológicas se estabilizaron tras una semana turbulenta para el sector de la inteligencia artificial, que ha sido el principal motor del mercado, con los inversores atentos a una intensa agenda de resultados corporativos y a la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal. * La mayoría de los sectores del S&P 500 registraron descensos el viernes, destacando las caídas en los grupos de consumo básico y financiero. * La próxima semana, cerca de un tercio de las firmas que componen el S&P 500 presentarán sus resultados trimestrales, entre ellas Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) y Amazon (AMZN.O) . Estas tres grandes compañías, clave en el desarrollo de la IA, verán cómo sus previsiones de gasto de capital son seguidas de cerca por Wall Street. * Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 39,57 puntos, o un 0,52%, a 7.623,86 puntos; el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) cedió 55,17 puntos, o un 0,21%, a 25.955,34 unidades; y el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) cayó 658,82 puntos, o un 1,25%, a 52.209,16 unidades. * Las acciones del sector de telecomunicaciones registraron caídas, lastrando al de servicios de comunicación, tras conocerse un informe que indicó que SpaceX (SPCX.O) estaba buscando miles de emplazamientos para antenas de telefonía móvil, con el fin de establecer un cuarto operador de telecomunicaciones inalámbricas. * El sector energético (.SPNY) subió, alcanzando un máximo histórico. El precio del crudo Brent tocó su nivel más alto desde finales de abril, después de que los ataques de los hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaran la preocupación por posibles interrupciones en el suministro energético proveniente de Oriente Medio. * Se espera que la Reserva Federal mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios cuando publique su comunicado de política monetaria el próximo miércoles. Sin embargo, los inversores buscarán con interés cualquier indicio sobre si el banco central estadounidense subirá los tipos en su reunión de diciembre. * Asimismo, Wall Street presta cada vez más atención a las elecciones de mitad de mandato del 3 de noviembre, que determinarán el control del Congreso de los Estados Unidos.

item.title: France Veillée d'armes avant une nouvelle journée de manifestations, le dispositif sécuritaire renforcé
item.description: La France se préparait vendredi à une nouvelle journée de manifestations à hauts risques samedi, une semaine après les violences et les pillages survenus en marge de défilés pour les conditions d'enseignement détériorées et contre la vie chère, obligeant l'exécutif à un sursaut.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La France se préparait vendredi à une nouvelle journée de manifestations à hauts risques samedi, une semaine après les violences et les pillages survenus en marge de défilés pour les conditions d'enseignement détériorées et contre la vie chère, obligeant l'exécutif à un sursaut. Comme le 17 octobre, plusieurs centaines de milliers de personnes pourraient défiler samedi dans tout le pays, selon des prévisions non confirmées par les autorités. Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, a annoncé la mobilisation de 70.000 membres des forces de sécurité intérieure - soit environ 10.000 de plus que la semaine dernière - dont des unités spécialisées comme le GIGN, la BRI et le RAID, en plus de la présence dans les gares et les aéroports de militaires du dispositif Sentinelle. "Nous serons intraitables", a-t-il dit lors d'un point de presse à son ministère. "On ne laissera rien passer." Outre les quelque 2.400 individus interpellés le 17 octobre, "près de 500 personnes" ont été arrêtées après investigations, a-t-il précisé. Après un conseil de défense et de sécurité dans la matinée, le président Emmanuel Macron a reçu dans l'après-midi des représentants des lycéens, mobilisés depuis plus d'un mois pour obtenir de meilleures conditions d'études et désormais rejoints par d'autres Français réclamant du pouvoir d'achat. "Ce dialogue qui a lieu alors que se clôt la phase de consultation des lycéens ouvre la voie aux annonces qui seront faites par le Premier ministre lundi prochain. Des décisions concrètes seront prises, pour le court comme le moyen terme", a déclaré l'entourage du chef de l'Etat. "Il a été question des conditions d’étude et de la nécessité de rénover le bâti scolaire, des rythmes scolaires et des emplois du temps qui requièrent des simplifications, de la meilleure prise en charge de la santé des jeunes, et des difficultés liées à l’orientation en fin de lycée", poursuit cette source, soulignant qu'Emmanuel Macron a exprimé le besoin d'une refonte en profondeur de Parcoursup, plateforme d'accès à l'enseignement supérieur. Le chef de l'Etat devait visiter en fin de journée une caserne de police dans le XIXe arrondissement de Paris pour témoigner "sa reconnaissance aux forces de sécurité intérieure mobilisées depuis le week-end dernier" et dire "sa confiance à l'ensemble des effectifs appelé à intervenir dans les prochains jours", a fait savoir l'Elysée. Le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, a confirmé dans la soirée que le gouvernement allait "bouger" sur Parcoursup, sans plus de précisions. JOURNÉE DE GRÈVE ET DE MANIFESTATIONS LE 5 NOVEMBRE Après les violences et le pillage de quelque 3.000 boutiques et magasins le 17 octobre, le chef de l'Etat a annoncé jeudi [USN:S8N3QT0LD TEXT:"l'interdiction"] des manifestations et regroupements sans "légitimité" et des "tracés alternatifs" pour protéger les centre-villes. A Paris, la préfecture de police a finalement interdit le parcours proposé pour le samedi par la CGT entre Bastille et Nation après l'avoir accepté dans un premier temps. Elle propose à la place "un tracé de porte d'Italie à porte de Vincennes via le boulevard des Maréchaux, pour une manifestation de 13 heures à 19 heures". Le défilé proposé par les "Gilets jaunes" entre Opéra et Bastille avait été interdit d'emblée. Les musées d'Orsay, de l'Orangerie, du Louvre, le musée Picasso seront fermés, ainsi que le Grand Palais où se devait se poursuivre ce week-end la foire annuelle d'art contemporain Art Basel Paris. A Limoges (Haute-Vienne), Sébastien Lecornu a appelé à la transparence sur ce qui s'est passé dans l'incendie criminel de la mairie samedi dernier, notant que "les faits sont particulièrement graves, plus graves que ce que l'on pensait". Aux côtés du maire de la ville, Guillaume Guérin, le chef du gouvernement a souligné que "ceux qui mis le feu sont responsables". "Ce sont des actes délibérés, planifiés", a-t-il dit, assurant que l'Etat allait reconstruire la mairie à l'identique et que le contribuable local ne payerait pas. S'agissant des manifestations de samedi, Sébastien Lecornu a déclaré que le "retour d'expérience avait été fait" après les violences qui ont émaillé la mobilisation du 17 octobre et que le dispositif prévu se serait pas le même que celui de la semaine passée. Il a ajouté que le niveau de menace restait élevé pour samedi avec notamment l'ultra gauche. Des préfectures ont interdit la tenue de manifestations à Lyon, Rouen, Le Havre, Nice, Chambéry, Le Mans ou encore Grenoble mais les choses pourraient encore évoluer en fonction des situations locales. Le préfet des Bouches-du-Rhône a ainsi annoncé dans l'après-midi qu'il autorisait la tenue, à Marseille, d'une manifestation à l'appel de la CGT. "Chaque préfet examine de très près les manifestations déclarées ou pas", a dit Laurent Nuñez, qui a évoqué de possibles défilés "en périphérie des centres-villes". Après une visite à [USN:L8N4690V5 TEXT:"Trappes"] dans les Yvelines, où une fusillade a fait un mort et quatre blessés, le ministre de l'Intérieur était attendu à Orléans pour y superviser les préparatifs de la manifestation de samedi. Entre 20.000 et 30.000 opposants venus de "toute la France", selon une prévision de la préfecture du Loiret, sont attendus à Orléans, ville de Jeanne d'Arc, pour un défilé hostile au Rassemblement national, qui y tient son congrès tout le week-end. La secrétaire générale de la CGT, Sophie Binet, le Premier secrétaire du Parti socialiste, Olivier Faure, et le maire La France insoumise de Saint-Denis (Seine-Saint-Denis), Bally Bagayoko, participeront à ce rassemblement sous haute protection policière qui partira à 10h30 de la cathédrale d'Orléans. Une journée nationale de grève et de manifestations, à l'appel de l'ensemble des organisations syndicales, est prévue le 5 novembre. C'est dans ce contexte tendu que le Rassemblement national, favori de l'élection présidentielle du printemps 2027, tient son congrès annuel à Orléans. Seul candidat à sa réélection, le président du parti Jordan Bardella sera reconduit samedi, et la candidate Marine Le Pen prononcera le lendemain un discours de lancement de sa campagne. Selon plusieurs sondages réalisés depuis le 17 octobre, la quadruple candidate à l'Elysée reste largement en tête des intentions de vote au premier tour, autour de 35%, loin devant le candidat de la France insoumise Jean-Luc Mélenchon, en position de se qualifier pour le second tour à environ 18%. Le leader insoumis a une courte avance sur d'autres candidats comme l'ancien Premier ministre Edouard Philippe et le gagnant de la primaire sociale-démocrate Raphaël Glucksmann.

item.title: Altibajos en plaza financiera de Argentina, ojos puestos en elección de Brasil
item.description: Los negocios financieros de Argentina mostraban un sesgo selectivo el viernes con las miradas enfocadas básicamente en temas de la política internacional, previo a elecciones presidenciales clave en el vecino Brasil y un nuevo incremento en el precio del petróleo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los negocios financieros de Argentina mostraban un sesgo selectivo el viernes con las miradas enfocadas básicamente en temas de la política internacional, previo a elecciones presidenciales clave en el vecino Brasil y un nuevo incremento en el precio del petróleo. Las acciones bursátiles fueron las estrellas de la ronda con una fuerte recuperación. Brasil, el principal socio comercial de Argentina, elige el domingo en [USN:L6N4670YH TEXT:"balotaje"] a su presidente, entre la reelección del socialista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y el referente liberal Flávio Bolsonaro, este último afín al mandatario nacional Javier Milei. Los últimos sondeos arrojan un reñido final. "En base a lo que pasó en la primera ronda, todo indicaría que Bolsonaro logre un ajustado triunfo y parte de los activos ya lo descuentan en precios, lo que consolidaría a la derecha en toda Sudamérica y le generaría un gran respaldo a Milei por su alineamiento con (el presidente estadounidense, Donald) Trump", dijo un agente corporativo de Bull Market Brokers. Acotó que "el enfrentamiento político de Milei con Lula es manifiesto y si la centroizquierda sigue gobernando en Brasil, podría ser un mal augurio de cara a necesarias nuevas alianzas económicas y financieras en la región, más cuando en 2027 hay elecciones presidenciales acá (en Argentina)". El flamante índice líder MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa porteña saltó un 4,29% al cierre en línea a los 'ADRs' de Nueva York y los bonos soberanos extrabursátiles promediaron un negativo del 0,2%, luego de perder el 1,31% y un 0,9% respectivamente el jueves cuando el riesgo país volvió a superar la línea de los 700 puntos básicos. Este referencial del banco JP.Morgan oscilaba ahora en las 710 unidades (1425 GMT), zona como máximo guarismo en un año. "Aunque las encuestas han mostrado un estrechamiento en la diferencia, Flávio Bolsonaro llega a la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales en Brasil este domingo como favorito, y su victoria parece estar, en gran medida, ya descontada por los mercados", reportó Capital Economics. Las presiones geopolíticas por el cruce bélico en Oriente Medio impulsa el alza general de precios, lo que aviva la posibilidad de un nuevo incremento en la tasa de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal a corto plazo. "La caída de las acciones tecnológicas pierde fuerza, aunque una nueva suba del petróleo limita el alivio en los mercados. El Brent toca su nivel más alto desde comienzos de mayo (unos 116 dólares) y puede agregar presiones inflacionarias", comentó Quantum Finanzas. El peso mayorista bajó un leve 0,1% a 1.529,5 por dólar , con la intervención diaria del banco central (BCRA) que acumuló compras por 270 millones de dólares en el transcurso de la semana, contabilizados los 42 millones adquiridos este viernes. Las reservas de la autoridad monetaria suman 50.203 millones de dólares en base al último dato oficial provisorio.

item.title: Soccer club Valencia says group backed by KKR founders buys 42% stake
item.description: Spanish soccer club Valencia CF said on Friday an investment group backed by KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis would buy a 42% stake in the club in a deal valuing it at €1.25 billion ($1.4 billion) including debt.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Spanish soccer club Valencia CF said on Friday an investment group backed by KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis would buy a 42% stake in the club in a deal valuing it at €1.25 billion ($1.4 billion) including debt.
